scope: Theorem 6.1 (Uniform upper embedding, companion theorem) of the manuscript “Tree Constructions for the l1 Distortion of Binary Edit Distance” (preprints/Tree-Constructions-for-the-l1-Distortion-of-Binary-Edit-Distance-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 099 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 696bf7848724daa2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants C > 0 and d0 ≥ 3 such that, for every finite alphabet Σ with |Σ| ≥ 2 and every integer d ≥ d0, there are an integer M ≥ 1 and one deterministic map f : Σ≤d → ℓM 1 satisfying ED(x, y) ≤ ∥f(x) − f(y)∥1 ≤ exp (︂ C √︁ log d log log d )︂ ED(x, y) (x, y ∈ Σ≤d ). Here ℓM 1 is RM with its usual ℓ1 norm. The domain includes the empty word, and ED is ordinary unit-cost insertion, deletion and substitution distance. The dimension may depend on Σ, d; the constants and threshold do not.
